gallery.description: Casa Batlló is a renowned building located in the centre of Barcelona and is one of Antoni Gaudí’s masterpieces.

gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo NobleFloor saloon.jpg
gallery.description: The saloon with its three interconnected spaces and large windows, providing panoramic views of Passeig de Gràcia and allowing the light to flood in, and its undulating ceiling, alluding to the power of the sea.

gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo dragon stairs.jpg
gallery.description: The Batlló family’s splendid private entrance hallway, accessed through a large door opening out onto the main communal hall. With a hallway that evokes the undersea grottos of Captain Nemo and a series of skylights that look like turtle shells, sinuously vaulted walls and a spectacular staircase, its fine carved hardwood bannister, representative of the coiled backbone of some vast beast.

gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo back dragon roof.jpg
gallery.description: At the top of the facade, the roof is in the shape of an animal’s back with large iridescent scales. The spine which forms the ornamental top is composed of huge spherical pieces of masonry in colours which change as you move along the roof-tree from one end to the other.

gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo inner courtyard bottom.jpg
gallery.description: In these yards, the walls are coated with pieces of ceramics and glass, some smooth and others standing out, in different shades of blue and the darkest shades are located on the top and the lightest shades are on the lower floors. gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo attic arcs.jpg
gallery.description: The attic was originally designed as a service area, and was once home to storage and laundry rooms. Even so, this area displays a dazzling Mediterranean beauty and an impressive elegance of form with Gaudí catenary arcs.

gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo inner courtyard.jpg
gallery.description: En estos patios, los muros se revisten con piezas de cerámica vidriada –algunas lisas y otras en volumen- en diferentes tonalidades de azul y donde las de mayor oscuridad se sitúan en la parte superior y las de color claro en los pisos inferiores. gallery.title: File:CasaBatllo rooftop chimneys dragon.jpg
gallery.description: In the whole of the roof stand the chimneys - a total of 27, arranged in four groups, of 6,10 meters of height, of helicoidal forms and topped by conical caps; Are lined with transparent glass in the central part and ceramic in the upper, and topped by transparent glass balls filled with sand of different colors.

La Illa de la Discòrdia, a row of houses on Passeig de Gràcia in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Spain, consisting of (left → right):
Casa Lleó Morera (Lluís Domènech i Montaner, 1905)
Casa Mulleras (Enric Sagnier, 1906)
Casa Amatller (Josep Puig i Cadafalch, 1900)
Casa Batlló (1877, remodelled by Antoni Gaudí, 1906)

gallery.title: File:Casa Batllo, Barcelona (40897276590).jpg
gallery.description:
Casa Batlló is a famous building located in the center of Barcelona and is a masterpiece designed by  Antoni Gaudí in 1904.
Several of his designs can be seen in and around Barcelona, including the amazing and as-yet unfinished church - the Sagrada Familia.

The facade of the Casa Batlló, seen here, is decorated with a colorful mosaic made of broken ceramic tiles and is said to evoke the surface of a lake with water lilies.  The entire building is quite amazing and is open to visitors.  Even the roof is a masterpiece
